Questions Review
Method

without isolating or justifying benefits of each method

Electric Small-Scale Rocket — Linsen et al. (2022, ICRA)
Questions Review
Method
Identify thrust/torque maps → optimal guidance
→ NMPC tracking and attitude stabilization
→ EKF mismatch estimation → Flight validation
Main
contribution Onboard integrated advanced GNC 
Limitation No controlled comparison with simpler controllers; 
No metrics from repeated runs
Shows integrated NMPC and online mismatch estimation can control
electric rocket during wind and landing tests, 
but does not isolate benefits over simpler control or 
measured actuator models.
R. Linsen, P. Listov, A. de Lajarte, R. Schwan, and C. N. Jones, “Optimal Thrust Vector Control of an Electric Small -Scale Rocket Prototype,”
Proc. IEEE ICRA, pp. 1996–2002, 2022. doi: 10.1109/ICRA46639.2022.9811938.
Spec 1.7 kg, 60 cm, 130s
Max Alt 3 m
Max Divert 2 m
Validation
Motion capture & 
wind test (3.1 m/s)
Outdoor Test

Questions Review
Method
Identify thrust and torque maps
→ Cascaded PID tracking → Control allocation

Main
contribution
Low-cost, open-source PX4/ROS 2 testbed

validation is limited to indoor motion capture

duration 53 s

platform construction and integration

Summary
Proven 
Low-cost electric TVC testbed flight
Coaxial and surrogate TVC 
architectures
Onboard optimal guidance and MPC
Indoor and outdoor demonstrations
Unresolved
Can it transfer to real rocket flight? 
Is performance robust under different 
conditions? 
Is performance repeatable across trials? 
Does it outperform tuned simple control? 
How much model fidelity is needed to 
predict performance?
